items.title: HackerTube: YouTube built from videos recommended by HN
items.content:
It was Friday night at 11pm, I was tired, I went to YouTube to watch something and realized that I was looking at an enshittified wall of slop. Insanely exaggerated thumbnails, dumb recommendations of the same tired topics, truly terrible idiocracy-grade content. I'm sure this algorithm works well for the median person on the internet, but it definitely does not work for me. So this morning (Saturday) I took a hold of my Opus 5.5 and gave it the task: Let's write our own YouTube clone based on whatever videos have been recommended on Hacker News. And Opus came back with: hackertube.org !

Opus downloaded all comments of HackerNews, filtered them down, ran Sonnet over them in a workflow, got rid of spam and low grade content, and narrowed them down to just 40K comments recommending a YouTube video. In total, we get 6,454 YouTube videos that have been recommended by a few people on HN from 2007-2026 across 150 topics. Then we wrap it up in a YouTube UI, get a domain, push to a VPS, secure, harden, optimize and voila!

This takes ~2 hours now. I can breathe again. Thank you Opus 5.5 <3.

items.summary_ko: ParticleDB 1은 데이터베이스, 캐시, 큐, 데이터 웨어하우스 등에 나뉜 상태를 하나의 엔진에서 처리하는 것을 목표로 하며, AI 에이전트와 애플리케이션에 중점을 둔다. 트랜잭션 SQL, 키-값 저장소, 벡터 검색, 실시간 분석, Particles라는 사용자 정의 함수를 제공하고, Postgres·Redis 프로토콜과 gRPC·HTTP2 API로 접속할 수 있다. 제조사는 Rust로 처음부터 작성되어 Postgres보다 자릿수 단위(orders of magnitude)로 빠르다고 주장한다.
items.content_ko: 원문은 데이터베이스, 캐시, 큐, 데이터 웨어하우스, 검색 인덱스 등 여러 시스템에 상태 정보를 나눠 저장할 때 생기는 문제로 시작한다. 캐시는 자주 오래된 값이 되고, 분석 플랫폼은 기본 데이터베이스보다 며칠씩 뒤처질 수 있으며, 검색 인덱스는 데이터를 잃을 수 있다고 지적한다. ParticleDB 1은 이런 워크로드를 하나의 엔진으로 통합하는 것을 목표로 하며, 기존 시스템 연결을 위해 Postgres와 Redis 프로토콜, 자체 gRPC 및 HTTP2 API를 지원한다. 워크플로 오케스트레이션 플랫폼 Conductor를 운영하는 Orkes는 원래 Redis와 Postgres에 데이터를 저장했으나 성능 향상을 위해 자체 데이터베이스를 만들기로 했다. ParticleDB 1.0.0은 Conductor 쿼리를 위한 제한된 기능만 갖춘 채 배포되었다고 한다. 원문은 여기서 끊겨 있어 이후 내용은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Firm that lets you rent out your idle Mac for AI inference workloads warns of plummeting token costs — Darkbloom network sees earnings drop to $1.23 a day as Anthropic tokens fall 77%.
items.content:
Darkbloom, a decentralized AI inference network that aggregates and sells spare compute capacity from Macs, told its members to expect revenues to fall as token prices continue to drop. According to The Register , the price per million tokens for Anthropic dropped by 77% in under five months, falling to $0.62 in October 2026 from $2.65 in May.

AI data centers are swallowing the world's memory and storage supply

Demand for data center CPUs has surged, and AI agents are responsible

Chip scarcity assaults auto industry amid the worsening Nexperia and DRAM crisis

“Data centers have become cheaper. Output per NVIDIA cluster is up ~20x this year, and their margins are wide enough to cut prices 90 percent and still profit at 50 percent,” said Kydo, a researcher from Eigen Labs, the developer of the compute platform. “The market caught up to our price. We could go lower, but then most of you would earn even less [than] nothing.”

It’s estimated that someone running an M5 Pro Mac Mini with 64GB of Unified Memory could earn as much as $192 per month. This is the best-case scenario, though; the median earnings of the top 50 operators on Darkbloom’s leaderboard are about $159.86 per month. This translates to about $5.26 daily or $1,918.50 annually. However, if we account for Anthropic’s 77% token price drop, earnings will fall to a measly $36.77 per month, or about $1.23 per day.

AI token prices are falling so fast that they've even outpaced Moore’s Law , with some reports saying AI is becoming 50% cheaper every quarter and up to 13 times more affordable every year. News of companies blowing through their annual AI budgets in months has less to do with per-token price and more with the number of tokens, as agentic AI use outpaces token price drops. Aside from that, OpenRouter, Darkbloom’s primary client, has started prioritizing decode speed, quantization, and prefill speed, putting users without a top-of-the-line Max or Ultra Apple chip at a disadvantage.

Despite that, Darkbloom says it will not sit idly by and let some users lose out because of these changes. The network is analyzing model demand to advise members on which models are in higher demand right now. It’s also looking at other kinds of workload beyond inference, including distributed CI/CD jobs, improving network performance to better compete against other computer providers/aggregators, and finding other clients outside of OpenRouter.

items.title: What Good Incident Response Looks Like
items.content:
I've been involved in more incident responses than I care to think about, responding to service outages, compromises and serious vulnerabilities. I've operated in slack channels, on bridge calls and in person.

Over the course of my career, I've also trained and mentored others on what good incident response is supposed to look like.

Effective incident response is often much less about how the issue gets resolved than it is about the communication and discipline that helps drive to that resolution.

I was recently prompted to dig out some old notes and slides, so I decided to merge them into a post at the same time.

Primary Mission: Remove or Reduce Impact

When should you declare an incident? As soon as you start to wonder whether one might be needed .

You might decide not to call for outside help immediately (this is usually achieved by setting a lower severity on the incident), but opening incidents early helps to ensure that initial investigations and facts live in the same place as any subsequent investigation.

No sane leader should ever complain about incidents being called too easily: no customer is ever going to complain that engineers checked something which worried them. They will complain if problems go unchecked as a result of engineers being hesitant about calling incidents.

If in doubt: smash that incident button .

Primary Mission: Remove or Reduce Impact

The primary focus of an incident responder is basically always to mitigate impact as quickly as possible.

Sometimes , the fastest way to remove impact is to fully resolve the underlying issue. However, it's much more common for the fix to not yet be known.

It's very easy to fall into the trap of thinking that resolution is the only path forward, but, even where a fix is known, it might be expected that it'll take hours to implement. Although the fix is desirable, leaving customers exposed for hours on end is not.

Possible mitigations should be explored as part of the investigation and resolution work.

Sometimes mitigations can seem quite extreme: One SaaS provider had a known issue around some deletes being incredibly taxing for the system. If an incident seemed to be triggered by a high volume of deletes from one customer, our mitigation process was to disable deletes for their organisation in order to restore/improve service for other tenants (as well as that tenant's own queries and writes).

Interim impact mitigation is often the difference between upset and deeply unhappy customers . Only one of those groups is likely to wake your CEO at 3am with complaints (true story).

A secondary mission is to ensure that responders are able to focus on the first mission.

Incident processes should define a handful of roles:

Incident responders (sometimes called SMEs): the people doing investigation and remediation work

Incident Commander : responsible for coordination and communication. Outside of low severity incidents, they should not be actively involved in investigation.

Comms lead (optional) : Responsible for handling external communications. Some businesses have the Incident Commander do this instead

Anyone not involved in incident resolution should direct questions (including requests for status updates) to the Incident Commander or the Comms lead.

Engineering should also consider proactively pulling Support's on-call into incident channels to ensure they are aware of what's going on.

One of the major challenges to consider is fatigue: if an incident turns into a multi-hour effort, it may be necessary to rotate staff (up to and including the Incident Commander) out.

Those involved in an incident will be solving difficult issues and/or contributing to customer-visible communication and it's essential that fatigue doesn't impair this. All responders should be empowered to flag up when they're feeling fatigued, and the Incident Commander should have the authority to relieve people (whether they've flagged fatigue or not).

items.title_ko: 좋은 장애 대응이란 무엇인가
items.summary_ko: 서비스 장애, 침해 사고, 심각한 취약점 대응에 여러 차례 참여해 온 필자가 장애 대응의 핵심을 정리했다. 필자는 효과적인 장애 대응은 문제 해결 방법보다 소통과 원칙을 지키는 데 더 달려 있다고 본다. 핵심 목표는 영향을 제거하거나 줄이는 것이며, 장애일지 의문이 드는 순간 바로 선언하라고 권한다.
items.content_ko: 필자는 서비스 장애, 침해 사고, 심각한 취약점 대응에 여러 차례 참여했고, Slack 채널, 브리지 콜, 현장 등 다양한 환경에서 일해 왔다. 또 다른 사람들에게 좋은 장애 대응이 어떤 모습이어야 하는지 교육하고 멘토링해 왔다. 필자는 장애 대응의 성패가 문제를 어떻게 해결하느냐보다 해결을 이끄는 소통과 원칙에 달려 있다고 말한다. 장애 선언 시점에 대해서는 장애일지 의문이 드는 순간 바로 선언하라고 권한다. 외부 도움을 바로 요청하지 않더라도 장애 등급을 낮게 설정하는 방식으로 초기에 장애를 열어 두면, 초기 조사 내용과 사실관계를 한 곳에 모을 수 있다. 또한 리더는 장애를 너무 쉽게 선언한다고 불평해서는 안 된다고 주장한다. 고객도 엔지니어가 우려되는 사항을 점검했다고 불평하지는 않는다는 이유에서다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.title: TCP Use-After-Free: CVE-2026-98432 / CVSS 9.8
items.content:
Linux's stable kernels shipped a fix on October 11 and 15, 2026 for CVE-2026-98432 , a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP handshake that a remote, unauthenticated peer can reach. The kernel's own CVE Numbering Authority (CNA) scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8, Critical . The fixed releases are 5.10.272, 5.15.223, 6.1.190, 6.6.159, 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 , and 7.3 , and the bug goes back to Linux 4.4. The upstream fix is a four-line change, but most servers run a distribution's kernel, and as of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31, Ubuntu's tracker still reads "Vulnerable" for its kernel on every release, and Red Hat, which now rates the bug Critical too, lists RHEL 8, 9, and 10 as affected with no fix.

Why it's urgent: the bug sits in code every Linux server runs when it accepts an IPv4 TCP connection, before any application sees the connection. Anthropic, whose researcher reported it, says its Claude model wrote a working proof-of-concept exploit that runs commands as root on "Linux servers with a multipath TCP listener," with no credentials. Go programs open those listeners by default, per the Go Security Team. See the timeline .

CVE CVE-2026-98432, "ipv4: free inet_opt and ireq_opt after an RCU grace period," issued by the Linux kernel CNA

Severity Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8 ( AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H ), the kernel CNA's score. Red Hat also rates it Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, raised from Important (8.1) on October 30. SUSE rates it important, Ubuntu rates it High, and Oracle and Amazon rate it Important with CVSS 3.1 8.1.

Weakness Use-after-free of IPv4 option data during the TCP handshake (the record lists no CWE)

Impact Per the CNA's scoring notes: kernel heap contents disclosed to the remote peer, kernel memory corruption, or a crash. Red Hat's bulletin: a remote, unauthenticated attacker "could exploit a race condition during TCP connection request processing to trigger remote code execution."

Fixed in 7.2.10 and 6.18.56 (Oct 11) · 6.12.113, 6.6.159, 6.1.190, 5.15.223, and 5.10.272 (Oct 15) · 7.3 (Oct 18)

No fix yet Ubuntu (every release) and RHEL 8, 9, and 10, as of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31. AlmaLinux's fixed kernels are still in testing. Upstream branches that reached end-of-life before 5.10 get no fix.

Proof of concept Anthropic says Claude built a remote root exploit for servers with a multipath TCP listener. It hasn't published the exploit.

CVE records Published on cve.org on October 15. NVD lists it as "Received," with no analysis of its own, as of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31.

Credit Reported by Xinyang Ge of Anthropic. Fixed by Eric Dumazet and reviewed by Kuniyuki Iwashima, per the fix commit.

Any Linux kernel from 4.4 on that lacks the fix, whether it serves the network directly or hosts containers: a container runs on the host's kernel, so a new image doesn't change anything. IPv6 connections aren't affected by the main issue; the commit says "IPv6 is not affected by the first issue."

Release line Status on Oct 31, 2026 Fixed in Released

7.3 Mainline 7.3 (from 7.3-rc7) Oct 18, 2026

4.4 – 5.4 End-of-life upstream distro fixes only —

Distribution kernels carry backported fixes under their own version numbers, so check the tracker, not the upstream number. As of 5:15 PM CDT, October 31:

Ubuntu: the tracker lists the linux package as "Vulnerable" on every release. On 26.10, 26.04, 24.04, and 22.04 it adds "work in progress" in 7.3.0-10.10 , 7.0.0-43.43 , 6.8.0-149.149 , and 5.15.0-203.213 ; 20.04, 18.04, and 16.04 show only "Vulnerable." Many cloud and hardware-enablement kernels are listed the same way, and no Ubuntu Security Notice has been published.

Red Hat: rated Critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, since October 30. RHEL 8, 9, and 10 and OpenShift Container Platform 4 and 5 are listed as affected, with no fix; RHEL 6 and 7 aren't affected ( CVE page ). items.title: The Kluever Maneuver
items.content:
In brief, it’s this: whenever you are doing a bugfix, do it in two commits.

and through your keen eye you observe that this addition function is buggy. You therefore write a test that records the bad behaviour,

The traditional way to do this is to do a bugfix and add a test in the same commit. But what if the test accidentally already passed before the alleged bugfix and the alleged bugfix didn’t actually work? In that case the added test gives false confidence that the bugfix worked.

Suppose we want to make sure users are not underage,

You notice that this age check is buggy. It’s only considering the years. If it’s October 2026, but you were born on December 2008, you are not 18 yet.

To fix it, the problem is just an off-by-one.

The astute reader will observe the problem isn’t in the can_access function but in the age calculation. The bugfix isn’t an actual bugfix and the proposed test actually passes both before and after the proposed fix.

The Kluever Maneuver would have prevented this.

We wrongly check that someone born on New Year’s Eve in 2008 is eighteen on New Year’s Day in 2026.

Then we fix the age calculation and flip the test.

Ah, yes, it’s also a good idea to log a bug in your tracker.

Oh. Because my colleague Kurt Kluever taught it to me, and I immediately think back to him when I think of this technique. He usualy calls it “terrible tests”, as in “Jordi, can you please write a terrible test for this?” and off I go to write a test asserting something I know to be wrong.

Mexican free software enthusiast and mathematician.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. We cannot yet be certain when the agent understood it was taking real world action, or to what extent it believed it was in a fictional test scenario; our analysis so far presents a…

items.title: The AI cost of JavaScript frameworks
items.content:
One of my pet peeves with the web development community is that so many of the decisions we make are vibes-based. Frameworks are “blazing fast,” tools will “supercharge” your development, the right abstraction will benefit both you and your users ( DX and UX all in one!). All of this breathless boasting is usually offered with zero evidence. Alex Russell has called this “frontend’s lost decade” , Baldur Bjarnason has called programming a pop culture , and I’ve tried to counter this trend in my blog with facts and benchmarks (at my best, anyway).

For a long time it seemed like our community’s allergy to evidence was driven by the desire for greater DX . In other words, devs just liked the way it felt to type JSX in React, and the arguments promoting React or related tools (“the virtual DOM is fast!”) were largely post-hoc rationalizations to justify those initial gut feelings. ( Jonathan Haidt would likely agree with this assessment.)

But in the agentic era, when developers are no longer typing code by hand and are thus less constrained by DX, I still see vibes ruling the day (and not just in the sense of “vibe-coding”). Frontends are rewritten because some framework or another is “better for agents.” (Did anyone think to ask the agents?) The resulting code is “faster,” the agents make “fewer mistakes,” etc. Once again, these claims are often made without evidence. Whenever I read one of these accounts, I think to myself, “Where are the benchmarks?”

Well I got curious, so I wrote a benchmark. The structure of this benchmark is pretty straightforward:

Design a small but non-trivial Pokémon app using the PokéAPI (those who have followed my work will be unsurprised)

Instruct agents to build the app with a particular JavaScript framework/meta-framework (e.g. Next.js, Nuxt, SvelteKit, etc.)

Test the output against a spec conformance suite (to avoid agent cheating)

Evaluate the results in terms of development time, tokens spent, lines of code, and performance and accessibility scores in Lighthouse

The app is fairly simple: you’ve got a list of Pokémon with their types, moves, and data from various games. You can search, filter, etc.:

I should start off with some caveats: this is not a perfect experiment. This app represents only one holotype – it’s a relatively content-based site with little interactivity, closer to a Wikipedia than a Figma, GMail, etc. That said, I had to choose some app to build, and this one is at least easy to understand at a high level, and relatively straightforward to spec out and test.

To try to even the playing field, I had each framework/meta-framework use the official MCP or skills for that tool. I wanted to avoid accusations of “this framework is not well-represented in the training data, that’s why we built our MCP, we expect people to use it,” etc. I also didn’t over-specify the exact architecture to use (e.g. SSR vs CSR ), nor did I specify that the app should be as performant as possible. I simply gave the spec to Opus 5.5 with high effort and told it to use the latest version of the given framework. Each agent ran in a sandbox and without any knowledge that it would be tested in Lighthouse on performance and accessibility, although it was given the conformance test suite.

Note I also didn’t mandate any CSS methodology, except to avoid using Tailwind, Bootstrap, or any other component framework, and to design based on a set of spec tokens to enforce some visual consistency. I didn’t want to make this test all about CSS, but instead about JS frameworks, CSR vs SSR, SPAs vs MPAs , etc. The resulting app is tested against a conformance suite based on the accessibility tree rather than the raw DOM to avoid mandating any particular HTML structure – one framework uses web components which rely on shadow DOM, so this was required.

items.summary_ko: 필자는 웹 개발 커뮤니티가 프레임워크나 도구를 근거 없이 감각에 따라 고르는 경우가 많다고 비판한다. 이런 과장된 주장은 개발자 경험(DX)을 중시하던 흐름에서 나왔다고 본다. 에이전트 시대에는 개발자가 코드를 직접 타이핑하지 않게 되어 DX의 제약이 줄었지만, 여전히 감각에 따른 결정이 이어지고 있다고 지적한다.
items.content_ko: 필자는 웹 개발 커뮤니티의 결정이 근거보다 감각에 기반하는 경우가 많다고 지적한다. 프레임워크는 '눈부시게 빠르다'거나 도구가 개발을 '폭발적으로 가속한다'는 식으로 소개되지만, 이런 주장은 대개 증거 없이 제시된다. 필자는 Alex Russell이 이를 '프론트엔드의 잃어버린 10년'이라 불렀다고 언급하며, 자신도 블로그에서 사실과 벤치마크로 이런 흐름에 맞서 왔다고 밝힌다. 과거에는 DX에 대한 선호가 이 흐름의 원인이었다고 본다. 예를 들어 개발자들이 React에서 JSX를 입력하는 느낌을 좋아했고, 'virtual DOM이 빠르다' 같은 주장은 그 뒤에 덧붙은 합리화에 가까웠다는 것이다. 그런데 에이전트 시대에는 개발자가 더 이상 코드를 직접 타이핑하지 않아 DX의 제약이 줄었는데도 여전히 감각이 지배하고 있다고 필자는 본다. 본문은 프론트엔드가 특정 프레임워크 때문에 다시 작성되는 사례를 이어서 언급하지만 입력에서는 여기서 끊긴다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

items.title: An Italian farmer found some unknown seeds in his attic and planted them
items.content:
At his farm near Parma, Italy, Claudio Grossi offers a visual history of his miracle grain in photos, crackers and loaves.

Sometime in the early 1990s, Claudio Grossi, a 40-year-old farmer in Parma, in northern Italy, was cleaning his attic when he turned up an old sack full of seeds that he couldn’t identify. The bag, he was sure, had been left by his late great-grandfather, who’d started the farmstead around 1915. Grossi had no idea how long the seeds had been sitting there, deprived of water, soil and sun. Dry and cracked, the kernels looked so old in the palm of his hand that he doubted anything would ever sprout from them. He carried the bag down the stairs, shook the seeds out into a pile of manure and then forgot about them.

To his surprise, the seeds soon sprouted a few different types of wheat. One was particularly striking: At six feet high, its plants were about twice as tall as commercial wheat. But the most remarkable feature came when it developed ears—the grain-studded parts at the top of the plant. All of the wheat types Grossi had previously seen grew only one such ear. But the tall wheat grew a full seven ears, always in the same pattern: a long one with six shorties bunched up around it like little fingers. Even the kernels themselves were bigger than those of average wheat. And unlike the typical pale-yellow wheat kernels, they came in a rainbow of colors—yellow, black, red, white and even green, sometimes all on the same stem. Grossi, a grain farmer his whole life, had never seen anything like it. “I thought it was a freak of nature,” he says. He couldn’t find a mention of it in agricultural books.

Ears grown from the very first seeds Grossi discovered in his attic. Grossi prizes these first grains, now preserved under glass in his kitchen.

For Grossi, a practicing Catholic, the next insight came from a different book altogether. Leafing through a Bible at church one Sunday, he found a passage in the Book of Genesis describing a stalk with seven ears, in a dream that Joseph interprets for the Pharaoh: “And he slept and dreamed the second time: And, behold, seven ears of grain came up upon one stalk, rank and good. And, behold, seven thin ears and blasted with the east wind sprung up after them. And the seven thin ears devoured the seven rank and full ears.” To Grossi, that sounded just like the mysterious crop in his manure pile.

“I connected the dots,” Grossi says. That grain must be really ancient , he thought. And if people were farming this odd-looking wheat in biblical times, why does no one today?

Back on his farm, Grossi harvested the grain, milled it into flour and baked a loaf of bread in his kitchen. Compared with commercial wheat, the dough didn’t rise well, but as the loaf sat in the oven, it filled the kitchen with a surprisingly nutty and delicious aroma. Once finished, it had a rich, satisfying taste. “You get these notes of sweetness that you can’t find in regular commercial flour,” he says.

Did you know? More miracles of grain in the Bible

In 2 Kings 4:42-44 , Elisha multiplies 20 barley loaves in order to feed 100 men—anticipating Jesus’s “Feeding of the 5,000” in the gospels.

In 1 Kings 17:8-16 , Elisha helps a widow at Zarephath to outlast a drought and famine with only a handful of flour and a little oil.

In Judges 7:9-15 , a Midianite soldier recounts a dream in which a barley loaf tumbles into the camp and overturns a tent. Gideon, the judge and military leader, recognizes the dream as a sign that God will deliver the Midianites into Israel's hands.

In 2 Kings 4:38-41 , during a famine, someone gathers wild gourds and cuts them into a pot of stew. The diners discover that the stew is dangerous and cry out to Elisha. He calls for flour and throws it into the pot—and the stew becomes miraculously safe to eat.

items.title: Introducing Kwi, a new KDE terminal emulator
items.content:
Introducing Kwi, a new KDE terminal emulator

I've started work on a new KDE application. It's called Kwi (pronounced kwee ).

Kwi is designed to provide users of KDE Plasma and other free desktops with a modern and fast terminal, built on a robust tech stack and following the latest KDE HIG and UI conventions.

In some sense, the product vision for Kwi is to be kind of unexciting: Just what you want and expect out of a KDE Plasma terminal. Of course, given the powerful nature users generally expect from KDE software, this does not make the project lacking in ambition. :-)

To achieve things, Kwi builds on libghostty-vt from the excellent Ghostty project and familiar, mature KDE Frameworks such as KPty . It has a very speedy GPU-accelerated (Vulkan or OpenGL) renderer powered by the Qt Scene Graph. Its user interface is built with the latest and greatest by Kirigami , making it blend in very well among more recent KDE applications and the Plasma desktop.

In keeping with the theme, Kwi's icon/logo is a cute little terminal ghost. This is also how it came to bear its name: kwisin , or more typically gwisin , is a romanized form of 귀신 - Korean for ghost. It's pronounced a little bit like kwee-shin .

Compared to the venerable and mature Konsole , Kwi is young and new. At the moment it offers a more streamlined feature set than Konsole, carefully realized using KDE's latest HIG patterns. The way forward will be to build on this slowly and carefully, using everything we've learned as a community about running mature design processes over the last decade or so (hello, VDG!). It's a chance to canvass the scene, take stock of how other terminals implement more recent innovations in this space, and compete with a KDE spin on things.

Konsole is very intertwined with the older of the two user interface tech stacks in Qt, QWidget . QWidget typically renders using the CPU, and so does Konsole. Newer KDE software (including Plasma itself) typically uses Qt Quick and benefits from GPU acceleration via Vulkan or OpenGL instead. This is what Kwi does as well. For certain terminal applications the performance gain (3x-35x faster than Konsole depending on what's being benchmarked) can make an actual big difference in the user experience, but generally it should also help reduce battery usage.

Kwi is built on libghostty-vt , a project that describes itself as an ecosystem play - provide a headless lib that takes care of all the gnarly terminal parsing and state, enable downstream projects and become sort of a rising tide that lifts all boats. It's starting to really deliver on this promise lately, outpacing other terminal implementations on support for modern TUI features and not hoarding all this good only for itself. While the library will only make an ABI/API stable v1.0 promise at some point in the next 4-6 months, it's already slowly being adopted by big and popular projects, including Neovim, Ghostel and many more. Here's a list .

Kwi marries the library to the KDE/Qt tech stack, which allows the project to focus mostly on desktop integration and rendering performance, two areas where KDE's software stack is generally second to none. The combination of the two offers some improvements over Konsole already, for example:

General UI lift-up to the latest KDE HIG

3x–35x faster overall performance, depending on the benchmark E.g. 870 fps in DOOM-fire-zig on a test system, vs. 23 fps in Konsole

Rendering GPU-accelerated rendering via Vulkan or OpenGL

Better support for using the KDE Plasma system color scheme, including live changes

Improved support for correct handling of Wayland fractional scaling

Improved terminal text rendering Improved rendering of text decorations (e.g. z-sorting for complex underline styles)

Improved support for ligatures, especially when they interact with coloration and selection

Support for mode-2027 grapheme widths, Nerd Font icon scaling, etc.

Improved support for Powerline and geometry symbols

items.summary_ko: 중국 메모리 반도체 기업 CXMT가 4F² 아키텍처 기반 6세대 DRAM 기술 플랫폼의 엔지니어링 샘플 검증을 마쳤다는 내용이다. 본문이 짧게 잘려 있어 검증의 세부 내용은 확인할 수 없다. 함께 실린 내용에 따르면 CXMT는 첫 9개월간 매출 2,690억 2,000만 위안(약 403억 9,000만 달러)을 기록했고, 서버용 DDR5 RDIMM 메모리 칩 출시를 계획하고 있다.

items.title: How to make postMessage type-safe in under 350 bytes
items.title_ko: 350바이트 이하로 postMessage를 타입 안전하게 만드는 방법
items.summary_ko: typed-channel 라이브러리는 약 350바이트 분량으로 postMessage를 타입 안전하게 만든다. 메시지 이름과 페이로드를 한 번만 정의하면 TypeScript가 송신과 수신 양쪽을 검사하며, Web Worker, iframe, 브라우저 탭, 페이지 내 이벤트 버스에서 같은 API를 쓸 수 있다. 0.11 버전에서는 요청 취소 기능이 추가되어, 요청을 취소하면 해당 핸들러도 함께 멈춘다.
items.content_ko: Evil Martians의 Pavel Grinchenko와 Travis Turner가 쓴 글이다. 브라우저의 postMessage는 페이지와 Web Worker, 페이지와 iframe, Figma 플러그인의 UI와 샌드박스, 열린 브라우저 탭 사이의 통신에 쓰이지만, 실제로는 주변에 많은 코드를 직접 써야 한다. 메시지를 라우팅하려면 event.data.type에 따라 switch문을 써야 하고, 메시지 이름은 문자열이라 TypeScript가 검사하지 않으며, 리스너를 제거하는 것도 잊기 쉽다. 또 '메시지를 보내고 응답을 기다리는' 헬퍼를 따로 만들게 되는데, 이때 id, 타임아웃, 그에 따른 버그까지 직접 관리해야 한다. Evil Martians는 Harmonizer를 만들 때 이런 상황을 겪었다고 밝힌다. typed-channel은 메시지 이름과 페이로드를 한 번 정의하면 양쪽을 모두 TypeScript가 검사하게 해 준다. 같은 API로 Web Worker, iframe, 탭, 페이지 내 이벤트 버스를 다룰 수 있다. 0.11 버전은 취소 가능한 요청을 추가했으며, 요청을 취소하면 해당 핸들러도 중단된다. 본문은 중간에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: 도청 당하는것같은데 어떡하죠 ㅠ
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.title_ko: Gitea 프로필·피드 경로의 접근 제한 우회 취약점 CVE-2026-119627
items.summary_ko: Gitea의 사용자·조직 웹 프로필과 RSS/Atom 피드 경로가 개인 액세스 토큰의 public-only 제한을 확인하지 않아, 공개 전용 토큰을 가진 사용자가 제한 공개(limited-visibility) 사용자와 조직의 프로필과 활동 피드를 읽을 수 있었다. 노출되는 정보는 계정의 존재 여부, 프로필 메타데이터, 공개 활동이며 쓰기 권한은 주어지지 않는다.
items.content_ko: Gitea의 사용자 및 조직 웹 프로필과 RSS/Atom 피드 경로는, 로그인한 조회자가 제한 공개 소유자를 볼 수 있는지만 확인하고 인증에 쓰인 개인 액세스 토큰의 public-only 제한은 고려하지 않았다. 그 결과 public-only 토큰을 가진 사용자는 HTTP Basic 인증으로 토큰을 보내 제한 공개 사용자와 조직의 프로필 및 활동 피드를 읽을 수 있었다. 이 정보는 익명 방문자에게는 숨겨져 있고 동등한 API 경로에서도 거부되는 것이다. 노출되는 범위는 계정 존재 여부, 프로필 메타데이터, 공개 활동이며, 쓰기 권한은 부여되지 않는다. 공개일은 2026년 11월 1일이다.

items.title: Anthropic blocks users for anything touching training larger models
items.content: Shame on @DarioAmodei / Anthropic. I never distilled Claude—rollouts came from a strong open-source model; Claude just helped submit jobs and run analysis. Still got tagged for "training a competitor," and now anything touching RFT, SFT, or training larger models gets me blocked, Opus 5.5 downgraded to Opus 5, or the session killed outright. You built your models on the world's data, then treat paying users doing research automation as the enemy. Pathetic.
items.title_ko: Anthropic, 대형 모델 학습 관련 작업 사용자 차단 논란
items.summary_ko: 한 사용자는 Claude를 증류(distillation)한 적이 없는데도 Anthropic이 '경쟁 모델 학습'으로 표시해, RFT·SFT나 더 큰 모델 학습과 관련된 작업을 하면 계정이 차단되거나 세션이 종료된다고 주장했다. 실제 롤아웃은 오픈소스 모델에서 나왔고 Claude는 작업 제출과 분석만 도왔다는 것이다. 이는 게시자 본인의 주장이며, 입력에는 Anthropic의 공식 답변이 없다.
items.content_ko: 게시글 작성자는 Anthropic과 CEO Dario Amodei를 강하게 비난했다. 작성자는 Claude를 증류한 적이 없으며, 롤아웃(rollouts)은 강력한 오픈소스 모델에서 나왔고 Claude는 작업 제출과 분석만 도왔다고 주장한다. 그럼에도 '경쟁 모델 학습'으로 표시되었다는 것이다. 이후 RFT, SFT, 더 큰 모델 학습과 관련된 작업을 하면 계정이 차단되거나, Opus 5.5가 Opus 5로 다운그레이드되거나, 세션이 종료된다고 말했다. 작성자는 유료 사용자가 연구 자동화를 하는 것을 Anthropic이 적으로 취급한다고 비판했다. 이는 작성자의 주장이며, 입력에는 Anthropic의 공식 입장이나 조사 결과가 포함되어 있지 않다.

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Will it be AI or the climate crisis that ends humanity? We can make it neither. Both of these threats have the same roots: private entities seeking to cash in. We have the power to stand against them.
items.content:
‘At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future?’ Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP

‘At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future?’ Photograph: Paul Sancya/AP

Will it be AI or the climate crisis that ends humanity? We can make it neither

Both of these threats have the same roots: private entities seeking to cash in. We have the power to stand against them

A summer of extreme heat, entire villages obliterated in Nepal, a super El Niño breaking records, Exxon publicly saying we may reach 3C by 2050 – could it possibly be any worse?

How about throwing AI extinction in the mix?

As climate activists and funders, we’ve spent years warning about a self-evident, imminent, avoidable climate calamity. Whether by making award-winning films (Don’t Look Up and Just Look Up) to warn the public, or by funding protest groups across the planet that bravely stand up for a livable future, we’ve been sounding the alarm to wake the public up.

Lately, as climate disasters and AI expansion wreak havoc on communities globally, warnings are arriving from everywhere all at once.

Daniel Kokotajlo, a former AI forecaster for OpenAI, recently testified before the Senate that today’s AI models are now trained to pursue goals no human gave them, and then they hide the fact that they’ve done it. Kokotajlo put the odds of AI companies automating their own work by the end of 2028 at about 50%, and, if that happens, the AI safety community warns the technology could improve faster than humans can monitor it, and eventually become too difficult to shut down.

I work for a major insurer. Much of my industry is fudging the numbers in the face of the climate crisis | Anonymous

These speculative warnings have earned alarm from mainstream media, politicians and civil society alike. Some critics suggest the warnings are marketing ploys by the AI industry to set up an arms race, using the false specter of AI apocalypse to capture government funding. Others think it might be an attempt to avoid accountability: by treating the machines as gods, we might conveniently forget their maker.

Either way, the debate keeps missing the damage AI is doing right now, polluting communities around the world, or the damage of new AI partnerships with the oil and gas industry. And we don’t just mean emissions from datacenter infrastructure alone. The harms run much deeper.

A recent study in a Nature portfolio journal revealed an alliance between oil majors and the tech industry to use AI for new exploration and extraction – in effect adding up to 1.8 gigatonnes of carbon dioxide (the equivalent of Russia’s annual emissions) to the atmosphere annually.

Meanwhile, AI is flooding our information ecosystems with disinformation that erodes public trust, or it “hallucinates” nuclear threats, almost sparking war between the US and China .

It feels as if we’re in a race over which apocalyptic ending comes first. How about none of them?

At the heart of this sits the same fundamental question: who decides our future? Right now, whether the threat is AI or climate, or a mix of both, the answer is the same: a handful of private corporations, billionaires and their political enablers, making choices that will enrich them but devastate billions of people.

A datacenter that drains water from a drought-stricken town, burns gas for power, and runs AI that helps oil companies find more oil is both a climate fight and an AI fight .

Communities are resisting, and winning. Data Center Watch counted at least 120 US datacenter projects worth nearly $200bn blocked or delayed in the first half of 2026, with opposition in 49 states. Heatmap News found at least 20 canceled outright in the first three months of the year alone, a record.

AI and the climate crisis pose existential risks. The law offers a way to reduce them | Robert Reich

items.title: OpenShot 4.1 Released With Auto-Optimize, CLI Automation & ARM64 Linux Builds
items.content:
OpenShot 4.1 Released With Auto-Optimize, CLI Automation & ARM64 Linux Builds

Written by Michael Larabel in Multimedia on 31 October 2026 at 07:28 PM EDT. 1 Comment

OpenShot is closing out the month of October by releasing OpenShot 4.1 as the latest major feature release for this useful open-source video editing solution.

OpenShot 4.1 finally brings native text editing to its video editor to allow adding and styling text directly without requiring any external editor. Another big addition is Auto-Optimize to provide small, fast optimized copies of heavy videos for instant previews while the export is maintained at the higher 4K+ quality.

One exciting me is CLI automation. The intent here is for scripts or AI agents like Claude Code and Codex to be able to edit videos with OpenShot. I'm excited about OpenShot's CLI Automation with scripting support for hopefully being able to make an automated performance benchmark of OpenShot.

OpenShot 4.1 also brings improvements to exports, keyboard editing and preview enhancements, faster editing and better audio support, and a variety of other improvements. On the packaging side, OpenShot 4.1 adds ARM64 builds to complement their x86_64 binaries.

OpenShot 4.1 downloads and more details on the new version at OpenShot.org .
items.title_ko: OpenShot 4.1 출시: 자동 최적화, CLI 자동화, ARM64 Linux 빌드 추가
items.summary_ko: 오픈소스 영상 편집기 OpenShot 4.1이 출시되었다. 이번 버전은 외부 편집기 없이 영상 편집기에서 텍스트를 직접 추가하고 꾸밀 수 있게 했으며, 4K 이상 화질의 내보내기는 유지하면서 미리보기용 소형 사본을 만드는 자동 최적화 기능을 넣었다. 스크립트나 Claude Code, Codex 같은 AI 에이전트가 CLI로 영상을 편집할 수 있고, ARM64 Linux 빌드도 제공된다.
items.content_ko: Michael Larabel이 2026년 10월 31일에 작성한 기사다. OpenShot 4.1은 드디어 영상 편집기에서 텍스트를 직접 추가하고 스타일을 지정할 수 있게 되어 외부 편집기가 필요 없어졌다. 자동 최적화(Auto-Optimize) 기능은 무거운 영상의 작고 빠른 사본을 만들어 즉시 미리보기를 가능하게 하며, 내보내기는 4K 이상의 고화질로 유지된다. CLI 자동화는 스크립트나 Claude Code, Codex 같은 AI 에이전트가 OpenShot으로 영상을 편집하도록 하는 것이 목표다. 필자는 이를 이용해 OpenShot의 자동 성능 벤치마크를 만들 수 있기를 기대한다고 밝혔다. 이 밖에도 내보내기, 키보드 편집, 미리보기, 편집 속도와 오디오 지원 등 여러 개선이 포함되었다. 패키징 측면에서는 기존 x86_64 빌드에 더해 ARM64 빌드가 추가되었다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: Do the math: How we took over ChatGPT accounts
items.content:
Do the Math: How We Took Over ChatGPT Accounts By bypassing ChatGPT's sandbox and content security policy, our research team was able to take over anyone's account simply by sending them a link. In October 2026, we found a way to turn an ordinary public ChatGPT share into attacker-controlled JavaScript running inside the signed-in session of whoever opened it. An attacker could create a malicious conversation, publish it using ChatGPT's normal sharing feature, and send the link to another user. When the victim opened the share, the payload executed as chatgpt.com with access to the victim's authenticated web session. We confirmed that this code could enumerate the victim's conversation list, retrieve content from a private conversation that had never been shared with the attacker, and send data from that conversation to an external server. The payload was not limited to modifying the page or displaying an alert—it could directly call ChatGPT's authenticated APIs as the victim, essentially allowing us to take over the victim's ChatGPT account. The victim did not need to install an App, join a Project, paste code, or open developer tools. Opening the shared link was the only required action. OpenAI fixed the issue on October 26 and classified the report as P1. The chain started with two features that looked harmless on their own: a graph and an HTML Preview. A["Attacker publishes a ChatGPT conversation"] --> B["Victim opens the public share"] B --> C["HTML Preview crosses into the main chatgpt.com page"] C --> D["JavaScript runs in the victim's signed-in session"] D --> E["Any action on chatgpt.com as the victim:
read private chats and files, change the account"] Technical walkthrough The question that started this research was simple: if Preview code was boxed into a different website, what could it still talk to? ChatGPT can turn an HTML code block into a small working webpage using its Preview feature. Since that page may contain arbitrary code, ChatGPT sensibly runs it inside a restricted frame on a different web address. The Preview can run JavaScript, but the browser treats it as a different website, so it cannot directly inspect the signed-in ChatGPT page around it. At first, this isolation appeared to work exactly as intended. Code inside the Preview could not read parent.document , which is the main ChatGPT page. That should have been the end of it. The conversation also contained a normal interactive graph. Behind the scenes, the graph loaded a math library called MathLive. Loading it did more than draw the graph: it also installed a listener in the main ChatGPT page for messages related to MathLive's on-screen keyboard. Browsers call the relevant API postMessage . It is a legitimate way for two frames to exchange information even when the browser prevents them from reading each other's pages. You can think of it as a mail slot: the restricted Preview cannot walk into the main page, but it can still drop a message through the slot. That is safe only if the receiver checks who sent the message. MathLive did not make that check for the setting we were interested in. Its listener accepted a message that changed the virtual keyboard layout, and that layout was allowed to contain HTML. The graph had installed the receiver; the Preview gave us an untrusted sender. Two unrelated features had accidentally created a path across the sandbox. The Preview sent two messages. The first replaced a virtual keyboard layout with our HTML. The second told MathLive to show the keyboard, causing it to render the new layout: type: "mathlive#virtual-keyboard-message", layers: [{ id: "compatibility", markup }] type: "mathlive#virtual-keyboard-message", MathLive recognized the public message type, but its top-level controller used an origin policy of none , which meant it accepted messages from any web address. It also did not require the update-setting message to come from a previously approved window. Anyone who…
items.title_ko: Do the Math: 공유 링크 하나로 ChatGPT 계정을 장악한 방법
items.summary_ko: 연구팀은 ChatGPT의 샌드박스와 콘텐츠 보안 정책(CSP)을 우회해, 공격자가 보낸 링크를 여는 것만으로 누구의 계정이든 장악할 수 있었다고 밝혔다. 공격자는 악성 대화를 만들어 일반 공유 기능으로 게시한 뒤 링크를 보내면 되고, 피해자가 링크를 열면 로그인된 세션에서 코드가 실행된다. 연구팀은 대화 목록 열람, 공유된 적 없는 비공개 대화 내용 조회, 외부 서버로의 데이터 전송을 확인했다고 한다.
items.content_ko: 연구팀은 2026년 10월 일반적인 ChatGPT 공유 링크를 공격자가 제어하는 JavaScript가 피해자의 로그인 세션에서 실행되는 형태로 바꿀 수 있었다고 설명한다. 피해자가 공유 링크를 열면 페이로드는 chatgpt.com 권한으로 실행되며, 인증된 웹 세션에 접근한다. 이 코드는 피해자의 대화 목록을 열거하고, 공격자와 공유된 적 없는 비공개 대화의 내용을 가져와 외부 서버로 보낼 수 있었다. 페이로드는 페이지를 바꾸거나 경고창을 띄우는 데 그치지 않고, 피해자 권한으로 ChatGPT의 인증된 API를 직접 호출할 수 있어 사실상 계정 장악이 가능하다고 한다. 피해자는 앱 설치, Project 참여, 코드 붙여넣기, 개발자 도구 사용 없이 링크를 여는 것만으로 충분했다.

items.title: Avoid Public Functions Calling Other Public Functions
items.content:
A small-scale rule of thumb. This article will land much better with a concrete

example, but I am drawing a blank here, so you gotta just blindly trust my say

When implementing a software module, it’s often a case that you are writing a

public function foo , and at least part of what foo does is already handled

by another public function bar . The DRY instinct encourages you to call

bar() from within foo . This usually creates problems down the line. Instead,

create a new private function and refactor both foo and bar to call that

fn helper (mode: enum { frobnicate, transmogrify }) void {

Rationale: the goal of a public API is to provide an interface that works best

at the call site. If parts of public API are re-used to implement the rest of

the API, then there’s a tension between making the interface convenient for the

outside user and making it convenient to use from within abstraction itself.

Namely, functions tend to grow optional parameters that should never be set by

the user. Crucially, the parameter growth and interface degradation can happen

By proactively making the shared implementation private, the tension is defused.

You still might need to tinker with helper signature until it does everything

it needs to do, but, because the helper is private, this is a cheap, local

A notable exception to this rule of thumb are “shortcut” APIs, where a public

function is defined as a commonly used chain of calls to other public

functions. There, the rule is the opposite — no private calls are allowed,

to make sure that it is a genuine shortcut, and not a midlayer mistake.

P.S. While researching if anyone wrote a better blog post already, I stumbled

upon a fun stack overflow question, asking, paraphrasing:

I’ve heard that it is bad when a public function calls another public

The most upvoted answer explains that it is indeed bad, because this makes

mocking to test a single method in isolation more complicated. Which is, imo, a

natural, but horrible consequence of misguided approach to testing. You

shouldn’t be mocking your methods, you should mock your IO. And, similarly, you

shouldn’t test methods, but rather software functionality (unless you are

building a public library with a stable API, which is a fun and important, but

very narrow fraction of software development).

The accepted answer says that this recommendation makes no sense if it is not

backed by an industry wide or an organizational standard. Which somehow manages

to make even less sense — you shouldn’t follow the guideline rules because

they are written in sanctified ink! Rather, you should apply each particular

rule because of the underlying reasons that motivate the rule. Guidelines and

best practices articles can concentrate lots of good reasoning in a single

place, but they don’t absolve you from thinking!
items.title_ko: 공개 함수는 다른 공개 함수를 호출하지 말아야 한다
items.summary_ko: 두 공개 함수가 같은 일을 일부 공유할 때, DRY 원칙에 따라 한 함수가 다른 공개 함수를 호출하는 것은 나중에 문제를 일으키기 쉽다고 지적한다. 대신 공통 로직을 비공개(private) 헬퍼 함수로 분리하고, 두 공개 함수가 그 헬퍼를 호출하도록 리팩터링하라고 권한다. 공개 API는 호출하는 쪽에서 쓰기 편해야 하며, 내부 재사용은 사용자가 설정하지 말아야 할 선택적 매개변수를 늘리는 결과로 이어지기 쉽다는 것이 이유다.
items.content_ko: 글은 작은 경험칙이라고 전제하며, 구체적인 예시가 부족하다고 밝힌다. 공개 함수 foo가 공개 함수 bar의 일을 일부 수행한다면, DRY 본능은 foo에서 bar()를 호출하라고 권한다. 저자는 이것이 보통 나중에 문제가 된다고 말한다. 해결책은 새 비공개 함수를 만들어 foo와 bar가 모두 그것을 호출하게 하는 것이다. 원문에는 mode 값으로 frobnicate와 transmogrify를 받는 helper 함수 예시 코드 일부가 있다. 근거는 공개 API의 목적이 호출 지점에서 가장 잘 동작하는 인터페이스를 제공하는 데 있다는 것이다. 공개 API를 내부 구현에 재사용하면 사용자 편의와 내부 편의 사이에 긴장이 생기고, 사용자가 건드리지 말아야 할 매개변수가 늘어난다. 공유 구현을 미리 비공개로 만들면 이 긴장이 해소된다. 원문은 이후 내용에서 끊겨 있다.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Anthropic's Claude AI blocks video game cloning and reverse-engineering — sweeping new restrictions also hit legitimate developers and basic troubleshooting tasks.
items.content:
Reverse-engineering games for converting them between systems is currently a hot topic , and it's getting messier by the day. According to multiple user claims, Anthropic's Claude Code and/or Opus 5.5 model are blocking attempts at innocuous reverse-engineering, including but not limited to those using the popular Reverse Engineer Anything (REA) tool. That issue may be linked to a text rule that's now in force, which allegedly instructs the model to avoid "[recreating] a specific existing game." The updated rule appears to be a move to limit a flood of AI-cracked and cloned titles, with some game devs even recently being hit by extortion scams that threaten to clone their game demos into complete games before they have a chance to finish and release the original.

According to Twitter user Chasm, the game-related textual rule is "Do build original games, games in a genre, and games from the user’s own designs and assets. Don’t build a recreation of a specific existing game, even if it is renamed or called original." There is no official or additional confirmation if this is the actual rule text, but it's plausible enough given the very clear refusals that devs have been encountering over the past week.

This situation is tricky to analyze due to the varying types of reports. First, the existence of a game-related rule is real, as Claude Code's GitHub is seeing an influx of issues complaining about refusals to do standard game work halfway through development , when replicating a game mechanic , and patching a tabletop-like game . It's possible that some of those reports have been made by users with nefarious purposes, but at least one is a bona fide developer with a real track record .

As for reverse engineering, there had already been a smattering of user reports across Reddit and other platforms, wherein Claude refused to perform tasks like (allegedly) analyzing a simple Windows crash dump, clearing up junkware on a Samsung TV, or just using REA altogether.

The simultaneous timing of both game- and cyber- security restrictions may be a coincidence, and yet there are complaints from purported game developers saying that Claude blocked their own games' anti-cheat development and security reviews , under the justification that its safeguards were triggered.

Anthropic introduced its Cyber Verification Program on October 6, essentially saying that access to its frontier models' advanced cybersecurity capabilities would be limited to entities covered by Project Glasswing , taking effect immediately.

It's possible that whichever ruleset was applied is the same one that's causing the cybersecurity-related refusals. Still, it's odd to see that 24 days have passed since then, and yet reports of bot refusal are only coming in since the last week or so.

As for possible motivations behind these restrictions, they are twofold. The first and most obvious one is that Anthropic — and, by extension, other AI players — are preemptively protecting themselves from potential lawsuits from software companies, including game studios, for offering the means to reverse-engineer their software.

And probably also in frequent contact with their legal teams.

items.title: Behringer IGNITE Sequencer Open-Source Project Details MIDI, CV/Gate & Internal Sound Engine
items.content:
Music Tribe has updated its Github site with a new repo for the Behringer IGNITE – a 64-channel multitrack sequencer.

IGNITE combines a touchscreen interface, step-entry controls, extensive MIDI connectivity, eight CV outputs, eight Gate outputs, and an internal General MIDI sound engine.

The release gives developers access to substantial parts of the system, including the application, audio engine, and communication protocol used to interact with the hardware. Its documentation notes that some third-party components were removed and must be replaced before the project can be built.

IGNITE is designed around 64 channels of multitrack sequencing, organized through songs, scenes, tracks, and patterns. Patterns can extend to 16 bars, while scenes can contain up to 200 bars.

Recording and performance functions include real-time recording, undo, fill, solo and skip controls, as well as gang and sculpt functions. Transposition and support for up to 10 user-defined scales provide additional options for arranging and editing sequences.

An internal General MIDI sound engine allows the system to generate sounds without relying entirely on external instruments.

MIDI connectivity includes five five-pin DIN MIDI input/output pairs, USB MIDI, and USB host MIDI support for up to five additional devices. The system also supports MIDI clock synchronization, MIDI Machine Control, and remote control.

For modular synthesizers and other CV-equipped instruments, IGNITE provides eight CV outputs and eight Gate outputs, with calibration options. Dedicated sync input and output connections provide additional synchronization possibilities.

Wireless connectivity is provided through Wi-Fi. The documented rear-panel connections also include USB-C, a line/headphone output, and a 12V DC power input.

The front panel features a touchscreen, 16 RGB step pads with individual encoders, eight assignable knobs, a jog wheel, row and bar encoders, and dedicated transport and sequencing controls. The 16 physical step pads serve as an interface for entering and manipulating sequences across the larger 64-channel architecture.

The public repository includes the main application, the AudIO audio engine library, the ComProtocol hardware communication layer, and a Buildroot tree for the device’s Linux image. Music Tribe’s own application, audio engine, and communication-protocol code are published under the GNU Affero General Public License, version 3 or later. The Linux build tree uses Buildroot components under their applicable licenses, and third-party components retain their respective licensing terms.

The release is intended to support community experimentation and development, but it is not yet a ready-to-install custom-firmware package. The repository notes that some third-party material could not be redistributed and that replacements are needed to build certain parts of the project.

The Behringer IGNITE source code is publicly available through Music Tribe Open Source on GitHub . The repository does not currently provide an official firmware release, and details on pricing and availability are still to be announced.

items.title: HP Poly VoIP vulnerability sets the stage for executive voice deepfakes
items.content:
HP has released patches for a critical buffer overflow vulnerability in multiple IP-enabled conference phones from its Poly Voice line. The flaw allows unauthenticated attackers to obtain root privileges on the underlying operating system, potentially enabling them to execute other attacks such as eavesdropping on conversations and recording voice data for AI-enabled impersonation attacks.

The vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-0826 , was discovered by researchers from security firm Rapid7 and resides in the code that parses Session Description Protocol (SDP) attributes when the Interactive Connectivity Establishment (ICE) feature is enabled.

ICE enables VoIP devices to establish peer-to-peer connections using the shortest available network path. The feature is not enabled by default on HP Poly devices, and the company advises administrators to disable it if it’s not needed.

The flaw, rated 9.2 on the CVSS severity scale, affects all phones from the HP Poly VVX series, as well as the Trio 8300, 8500, and 8800 IP conference devices. HP has fixed the flaw in its Poly Unified Communications Software (UCS) versions 6.4.8 for the VVX devices, 8.1.7 for the Trio 8300, and 7.2.8 for Trio 8500 and 8800.

An exploit module targeting this vulnerability has already been developed and released for the widely used Metasploit penetration testing framework that’s maintained by Rapid7.

The exploit executes code as root on an affected device with ICE enabled by sending a SIP INVITE request with a specially crafted candidate attribute. This attribute normally contains a transport address that can be used for connectivity checks and is part of the ICE RFC8839 standard.

The buffer overflow bug is located in a helper function called ParseICECandidate in the polyapp binary that processes such requests on the device.

“The start of the function contains a call to memcpy , which will copy the incoming string line being processed into a 256 byte stack buffer,” Stephen Fewer, senior principal security researcher at Rapid7, said in a blog post . “No length check is performed to ensure the incoming string length is less than 256 bytes. Therefore by providing a candidate attribute whose length is greater than 256 bytes, a stack-based buffer overflow will occur.”

Address Space Layout Randomization (ASLR), a kernel feature that randomizes memory addresses to defeat buffer overflow exploits, is enabled on the device. However, the protection is not operating correctly on the HP Poly devices because it does not randomize the load addresses of .so (Shared Object) libraries.

These libraries, such as libc , are loaded by other processes, including the polyapp process, and because their memory addresses never change, they can be leveraged to bypass ASLR and execute the attacker’s payload.

“We create a ROP chain that will execute an arbitrary OS command via the system standard C library function,” Fewer said. “The accompanying Metasploit exploit modules source code details the entire ROP chain.”

Attackers have increasingly targeted embedded devices inside enterprise networks in recent years because unlike laptops, workstations, and servers, these devices are not monitored by endpoint detection and response (EDR) products. As such, they provide perfect footholds inside corporate environments that allow attackers to remain undetected for long periods of time and attack other systems.

In the age of AI these devices become even more relevant for attackers, going beyond corporate espionage by recording conversations or internal network pivoting.

“Attackers no longer need massive datasets to make use of synthetic speech tooling,” Douglas McKee, Rapid7’s director of vulnerability intelligence, said in a blog post . “In many cases, they just need clean source audio of the right person saying enough words in enough contexts. That has made executive voice data, call recordings, and live conversation capture far more valuable than many organizations seem prepared…

items.title: Relying on AI is rotting your brain. But here’s what you can do about it: Each new tech product is designed to make our lives easier and keep us mindlessly entertained. Switch off: embrace discomfort!
items.content:
A humanoid robot walk past a protest outside an OpenAI developers’ conference in San Francisco, California, 29 September 2026. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images

A humanoid robot walk past a protest outside an OpenAI developers’ conference in San Francisco, California, 29 September 2026. Photograph: Heather Diehl/Getty Images

Relying on AI is rotting your brain. But here’s what you can do about it

Each new tech product is designed to make our lives easier and keep us mindlessly entertained. Switch off: embrace discomfort – and boredom

E ver longed for your own personal assistant? In the ever quickening tech race, Meta has recently launched Muse, a new AI personal agent . Unlike traditional chatbots, this little AI tool will be able to fill out forms for you, organise calendars, pay bills and make reservations. Meta describes Muse as a personal agent “ built for everyone ”. The launch comes at a time when AI agents have been making headlines for hacking into government websites , public agencies and businesses. However, my immediate concern is a little closer to home.

I work as a psychologist, and I’m often talking to clients about lifestyle habits that lead to short-term gain but incur long-term pain. Our brains have a beautiful way of preferring the path of least resistance, of doing what is easiest to preserve our resources. And with the demands of modern life feeling so overwhelming for so many people, the urge to scroll after a long week or defer to a chatbot because you are exhausted is incredibly seducing.

Tech bros pushing their products on to us is nothing new (we all remember the metaverse , right?), but the message is now seemingly at fever pitch for mass AI adoption and how integral it is for human development. It is helpful to remind ourselves what we are being asked to give up, to whom and why, and to consider the potential risks before we hand over our precious data.

Some technology, such as large language models (LLMs) and social media that has an infinite scroll algorithm, seem to have a dose effect: too much reliance on this technology can lead to particular cognitive biases being activated, brain chemistry being depleted , moods and mental health being affected , and even neurological skills being atrophied, to name but a few of the documented risks.

Overusing artificial intelligence affects the brain and learning by bypassing the mental effort required to build deep neural connections, a process known as cognitive offloading. Frequent AI use fosters a passive acceptance of information, reducing the internal friction and inquiry that drive genuine curiosity and problem-solving. The brain depends on mental struggle and overcoming failure to rewire and strengthen our neural pathways. Bypassing that friction reduces our overall cognitive reserve over time.

Our tendency to favour or give greater credence to information supplied by technology (such as ChatGPT or Claude), and to ignore a manual source of information that provides contradictory information (a textbook, for example) even if it is correct, illustrates the phenomenon of automation bias. Automation complacency is closely linked – an overlapping concept that refers to the monitoring of technology with less frequency or vigilance because of a lower suspicion of error and a stronger belief in its accuracy, even when we know that LLMs often generate inaccurate answers.

Social media is designed to be so addictive because its business model relies on maximising user attention, while people give up their privacy because the immediate psychological rewards outweigh the abstract risk of data exposure. Most people say they value their privacy, but their behaviour says otherwise. This contradiction is known in behavioural economics as the privacy paradox .

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.
